extracted.intended_audience: university and nonprofit technology transfer officers, small business contractors, patent administrators, and federal agency officials implementing Bayh-Dole patent rights clauses
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory and contractual standards governing ownership, disclosure, filing, licensing, march-in, reporting, confidentiality, and subcontracting of inventions arising under federally funded contracts (Bayh-Dole implementation and the standard patent rights clause).

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiation of march-in proceeding and notice requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A march-in proceeding shall be initiated by issuance of a written notice by the agency to the contractor and its assignee or exclusive licensee stating that the agency is considering the exercise of march-in rights, stating reasons sufficient to put the contractor on notice of the facts, specifying the field(s) of use under consideration, and advising the contractor of its rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The determination to exercise march-in rights shall be made by the head of the agency or his or her designee. The notice must identify facts and fields of use and refer to supplemental agency regulations where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor opportunity to comment before agency proceeds
rubrics_metrics.description: If the agency publishes notice of intent to consider march-in rights, it must provide a comment period (30 days) for receipt of comments from the contractor; if a comment is received within 30 days or if the agency has not yet initiated procedures, the agency must, within 60 days after it receives the comment, either initiate march-in procedures or notify the contractor it will not pursue march-in on the available information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no comments are received within 30 days, the agency may proceed at its discretion with the march-in procedures. Timelines: 30-day comment window, 60-day agency action after comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor right to submit opposition and raise factual disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 30 days after receipt of written notice of march-in, the contractor (assignee/exclusive licensee) may submit information or argument in opposition, including specific information that raises a genuine dispute over the material facts upon which the march-in is based.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a genuine dispute is raised, the head of the agency or designee shall undertake or refer the matter for fact-finding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fact-finding procedures for march-in
rubrics_metrics.description: Fact-finding shall be conducted in accordance with agency-established procedures that are as informal as practicable and consistent with fundamental fairness, affording the contractor opportunity to appear with counsel, submit documentary evidence, present witnesses, and confront agency-presented persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A transcribed record shall be made and be available at cost; the requirement for a transcription may be waived by mutual agreement. Portions involving utilization or efforts to obtain utilization by contractor/assignee/licensees shall be closed to the public. 35 U.S.C. 202(c)(5) prohibits disclosure of such information outside government except with contractor authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision-making standards and timeline after fact-finding
rubrics_metrics.description: The official conducting fact-finding shall prepare written findings of fact and a recommended determination transmitted promptly to the agency head or designee; the contractor and agency have 30 days to submit written arguments and may request oral arguments before the deciding official.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The head of the agency shall base determination on facts found and other record information; in fact-finding cases the head may reject only facts found to be clearly erroneous and must explicitly state basis for contrary findings. Written notice of determination must be sent by certified or registered mail within 90 days after completion of fact-finding or 90 days after oral arguments, whichever is later; otherwise proceedings are deemed terminated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency ability to terminate march-in proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may, at any time, terminate a march-in proceeding if it is satisfied that it does not wish to exercise march-in rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Termination may occur prior to exhaustion of the process; agencies may also issue supplemental procedures not inconsistent with the part for conduct of march-in proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: March-in applicability to inventors retaining title
rubrics_metrics.description: The march-in procedures apply to inventors receiving title under 35 U.S.C. 202(d); for this purpose the term 'contractor' includes the inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All march-in procedural protections and timelines apply when the inventor, rather than an organizational contractor, holds title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small business preference obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: Contractors are expected to use efforts reasonable under the circumstances to attract small business licensees and to give preference to small business firms that meet the clause standard over other applicants for licenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: What constitutes reasonable efforts varies with circumstances, nature, duration, and expense of efforts needed. The clause is not intended to prevent nonprofit organizations from providing larger firms a right of first refusal in long-term arrangements where seeking small business preference would be unreasonable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small business complaint and Secretary's informal investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Small business firms believing a nonprofit is not meeting its obligations under the small business preference clause may report concerns to the Secretary, who may undertake informal investigation and discussions to improve the nonprofit's efforts, but will not intervene in ongoing negotiations or contractor licensing decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigations and discussions shall coordinate with interested agencies including SBA; for GOCO contracts, coordinate with agency responsible for facility before discussions with contractor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting on utilization: format and Paperwork Reduction Act compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies have the right to receive periodic reports from the contractor on utilization of inventions; agencies should accept such information in the format the contractor normally prepares for internal purposes and avoid prescribing forms; any forms or questionnaires must comply with the Paperwork Reduction Act and copies sent to the Secretary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept contractor's customary format to the extent feasible; avoid creating burdensome standardized forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of utilization reports
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with 35 U.S.C. 202(c)(5), agencies shall not disclose such utilization information to persons outside the government; contractors should provide confidential markings to help prevent inadvertent release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must protect reports from external release, consistent with statutory limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for contractor employee inventor retention of rights
rubrics_metrics.description: When agencies allow an employee/inventor of the contractor to retain rights under 35 U.S.C. 202(d), the agency will impose at least the conditions that would apply to a small business firm contractor under specified clause paragraphs (d)(1) and (3); (f)(4); (h); (i); and (j) of §401.14(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency may impose similar obligations on inventor-retained-title situations to ensure consistent obligations as with small business contractors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government assignment to contractor of government-employee invention rights
rubrics_metrics.description: When a Federal agency transfers or reassigns rights it acquired in a subject invention from an employee to the contractor (35 U.S.C. 202(e)), the assignment will be subject to the same conditions that apply to the contractor under the patent rights clause of its funding agreement; agencies may add additional consistent conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional agency conditions are permitted only if consistent with 35 U.S.C. 201-206.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency written statement required when taking specified actions (appeals precursor)
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency official initially authorized to take certain actions (refusal to grant an extension, request for conveyance of title, refusal to grant waiver, refusal to approve assignment, refusal to grant extension of exclusive license period) must provide the contractor with a written statement of the basis for the action at the time it is taken, including relevant facts relied upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This written statement is a prerequisite to the contractor's right to appeal per agency procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency appeals procedures and scope of review
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall establish and publish procedures under which the actions listed (in the prior criterion) may be appealed to the head of the agency or designee; review shall consider both factual and legal basis for the actions and consistency with policy and objectives of 35 U.S.C. 200-206.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals review examines substantive and procedural consistency with statutory policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals fact-finding standards and due process
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals procedures shall include administrative due process procedures and standards for fact-finding at least comparable to those set forth in §401.6(e)-(g) whenever there is a dispute as to the factual basis for an agency request for conveyance of title, including disputes over whether an invention is a subject invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If actions are subject to the Contract Disputes Act, procedures under that Act will satisfy §401.11(c)-(d) requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing of contractor-owned background patents to third parties — approval requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A funding agreement will not contain a provision allowing an agency to require licensing to third parties of inventions owned by the contractor that are not subject inventions unless the provision has been approved by the agency head and a written justification has been signed by the agency head; the provision must clearly state whether licensing may be required in connection with practice of a subject invention, a specified work object, or both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency head may not delegate authority to approve such provisions or to sign required justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions under which agency may require licensing of background patents
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency will not require licensing of third-party background patents unless the agency head determines that (a) use of the invention by others is necessary for practice of a subject invention or for use of a work object of the funding agreement, and (b) such action is necessary to achieve practical application of the subject invention or work object; determination on the record after opportunity for an agency hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contractor must be promptly notified by certified or registered mail; judicial review actions must be brought within 60 days after notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of single agency for administration when subject invention involves multiple agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: When a subject invention is made under funding agreements of more than one agency, at the request of the contractor or on agencies' initiative, the agencies shall designate one agency as responsible for administration of the government's rights in the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designation simplifies administration and avoids conflicting demands across agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt agency approvals for nonprofit requests absent significant reason
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall promptly grant, unless there is a significant reason not to, a request by a nonprofit organization under paragraph (k)(2) for exclusive license duration approval and shall promptly approve assignments by a nonprofit to a patent-management organization as required by clause paragraph (k)(1), subject to the same policy for similar prior patent clauses or waivers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reflects amended 35 U.S.C. 202(c)(7) eliminating duration limitation and aligns older institutional agreements with current policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality protection of invention disclosures and patent applications re FOIA
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should protect confidentiality of invention disclosures, patent applications, and utilization reports to the extent permitted by 35 U.S.C. 205 or other laws; generally agencies shall not disclose information disclosing a subject invention under FOIA for a reasonable time to allow a patent application to be filed, and shall not disclose copies of patent application documents to third parties under FOIA for 18 months from the filing date (with exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasonable time for small business/nonprofit equals the time during which an initial patent application may be filed under paragraph (c) of the standard clause; disclosures may be released earlier if published elsewhere or if contractor elected not to retain title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication programs and exclusion of invention disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies' publication programs encouraging dissemination of contractor-supported work should not include disclosures of inventions submitted pursuant to patent rights clauses, except in circumstances where FOIA release would be authorized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If contractor notifies agency that a report contains invention disclosure, agency should use reasonable efforts to restrict publication for six months from receipt or until initial patent application filing; agencies retain discretion to delay longer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: 'Invention'
rubrics_metrics.description: "Invention" means any invention or discovery which is or may be patentable or otherwise protectable under Title 35 U.S.C., or any novel variety of plant protectable under the Plant Variety Protection Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad statutory definition to encompass patentable subject matter and plant varieties where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: 'Subject invention'
rubrics_metrics.description: "Subject invention" means any invention of the contractor conceived or first actually reduced to practice in the performance of work under the contract (for a plant variety, the date of determination must occur during contract performance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determines the scope of rights and obligations under the standard clause; conception or first actual reduction to practice during contract performance is key.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: 'Practical Application'
rubrics_metrics.description: "Practical Application" means to manufacture (composition/product), to practice (process/method), or to operate (machine/system) under such conditions as to establish that the invention is being utilized and that its benefits are available to the public on reasonable terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical application is the benchmark for whether contractor has achieved utilization sufficient to avoid revocation or march-in.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: 'Made'
rubrics_metrics.description: "Made" means the conception or first actual reduction to practice of such invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in determining whether an invention is a 'subject invention' for clause application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: 'Small Business Firm' and applicable size standards
rubrics_metrics.description: "Small Business Firm" means a small business concern as defined in Pub.L. 85-536 and implementing SBA regulations; size standards for government procurement and subcontracting will be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites relevant CFR sections for applicable size standards (13 CFR 121.3-8 and 121.3-12).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: 'Nonprofit Organization'
rubrics_metrics.description: "Nonprofit Organization" means a university or other institution of higher education or an organization described in 26 U.S.C. 501(c)(3) and exempt under 501(a), or any nonprofit scientific or educational organization qualified under state statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines entities eligible for nonprofit-specific provisions in clause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of principal rights
rubrics_metrics.description: The Contractor may retain entire right, title, and interest worldwide to each subject invention subject to clause provisions and 35 U.S.C. 203; where contractor retains title the Federal government shall have a nonexclusive, nontransferable, irrevocable, paid-up license to practice or have practiced for or on behalf of the United States the subject invention throughout the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contractor retention of title is the default; government retains an unlimited by-field license for government use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invention disclosure content and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The contractor will disclose each subject invention to the Federal Agency within two months after the inventor discloses it in writing to contractor personnel responsible for patent matters; disclosure shall be a written report identifying the contract and inventor(s) and be sufficiently complete in technical detail to convey a clear understanding of nature, purpose, operation, and characteristics to the extent known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure must identify any publication, on-sale or public use and whether manuscript describing invention has been submitted or accepted; contractor must promptly notify agency after acceptance, on-sale, or public use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election of title timing and shortened election windows
rubrics_metrics.description: The contractor will elect in writing whether to retain title by notifying the Federal agency within two years of disclosure; however when publication/on-sale/public use has initiated the one-year statutory period for US patent protection, the period for election may be shortened by the agency to a date no more than 60 days prior to end of statutory period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key timeline: typical two-year election window, but shortened to protect patent rights if public disclosure triggers statutory bars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing initial patent application timing and foreign filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Contractor will file its initial patent application on subject invention to which it elects title within one year after election or earlier if required to avoid statutory bar; contractor will file in additional countries/international patent offices within ten months of the corresponding initial application or six months from date permission is granted by the Commissioner where prior Secrecy Order prohibited foreign filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contractor must monitor statutory bars and Secrecy Orders; foreign filing timing tied to US filing and to PTO permissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency discretion to grant extensions of disclosure/election/filing times
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for extension of time for disclosure, election, and filing may, at agency discretion, be granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contractors should request extension with justification; agency has discretion but may grant for good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circumstances when government may obtain title
rubrics_metrics.description: The contractor will convey title to the Federal agency upon written request if (1) contractor fails to disclose or elect within specified times or elects not to retain title (agency may request title within 60 days after learning of failure); (2) in countries where contractor fails to file within specified times (with exception if filed before agency written request); or (3) in any country where contractor decides not to continue prosecution, pay maintenance fees, or defend in reexamination/opposition proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency request for title is time-limited (60 days after learning of failure to disclose/elect). Filing after specified times but before agency request allows contractor to retain title in that country.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum rights to contractor when government obtains title
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Government obtains title, the contractor retains a nonexclusive royalty-free license throughout the world in each subject invention (except if contractor failed to disclose within the specified times); the license extends to domestic subsidiaries and affiliates and includes right to grant sublicenses to the extent contractor was legally obligated to do so at contract award; license transferable only with Federal agency approval except to successor of that party's business to which the invention pertains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves contractor's limited ongoing rights while enabling government ownership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation or modification of contractor license to achieve practical application
rubrics_metrics.description: The contractor's domestic license may be revoked or modified by the funding agency to the extent necessary to achieve expeditious practical application pursuant to an application for an exclusive license; license will not be revoked in any field or geography where contractor has achieved practical application and continues to make benefits reasonably accessible to the public; foreign license revocation/modification is at agency discretion where practical application not achieved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revocation/modification linked to practical application performance; agency must follow procedural protections including notice and opportunity to show cause and appeal rights under 37 CFR Part 404.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures before revocation/modification and appeal rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Before revocation/modification the agency will furnish written notice of intention and allow the contractor thirty days (or other authorized time for good cause) to show cause why license should not be revoked or modified; contractor has the right to appeal per 37 CFR Part 404 and agency regulations regarding licensing of Government-owned inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides procedural due process and routes for challenging agency licensing decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor obligations to protect government's interest (instruments and employee disclosures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contractor agrees to execute and promptly deliver all instruments necessary to establish/confirm Government rights and to convey title when requested; contractor must require employees (other than clerical/nontechnical) to disclose promptly in writing each subject invention to personnel responsible for patent matters in a suggested format and to execute all papers necessary to file patent applications and establish government rights; contractor shall instruct such employees through agreements or education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure format should at minimum require information in clause (c)(1); contractor must ensure timely internal reporting to comply with statutory bars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of decisions to discontinue prosecution or maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: The contractor will notify the Federal agency of any decisions not to continue prosecution, pay maintenance fees, or defend in reexamination/opposition in any country not less than thirty days before the expiration of the response period required by the relevant patent office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advance notice gives agency time to decide whether to request title or take other action to protect government interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent application government support statement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Contractor agrees to include within the specification of any U.S. patent application and any issuing patent covering a subject invention the statement: 'This invention was made with government support under (identify the contract) awarded by (identify the Federal agency). The government has certain rights in the invention.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statement notifies the PTO and public of government involvement and rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcontract clause inclusion for experimental/developmental/research work
rubrics_metrics.description: The contractor will include this patent rights clause, suitably modified to identify the parties, in all subcontracts, regardless of tier, for experimental, developmental or research work performed by a small business firm or domestic nonprofit organization; the subcontractor will retain all rights provided for the contractor, and the contractor will not obtain rights in subcontractor's subject inventions as consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures pass-through of patent rights protections and obligations down the subcontract chain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent rights clauses in other subcontracts and contract-law effect
rubrics_metrics.description: The contractor will include required patent rights clauses in all other subcontracts for experimental/developmental/research work (cite agency implementing regs/FAR); when prime award was a contract, the mutual obligations of the parties created by this clause constitute a contract between subcontractor and the Federal agency with respect to matters covered by the clause (not intended to confer Contract Disputes Act jurisdiction regarding paragraph (j)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserves enforceability of patent obligations against subcontractors while noting limits on dispute jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting on utilization under the clause
rubrics_metrics.description: Contractor agrees to submit, on request, periodic reports no more frequently than annually on utilization of a subject invention or efforts at obtaining utilization by the contractor, licensees or assignees; reports shall include development status, date of first commercial sale/use, gross royalties received, and other data agency may reasonably specify. Additional reports may be requested in connection with any march-in proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As required by 35 U.S.C. 202(c)(5), the agency will not disclose such information to persons outside government without contractor permission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for United States industry in exclusive licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: Contractor agrees that neither it nor any assignee will grant any person exclusive right to use or sell any subject invention in the U.S. unless such person agrees that products embodying the subject invention will be manufactured substantially in the United States; requirement may be waived by agency upon contractor showing reasonable but unsuccessful efforts to grant licenses on similar terms to domestic manufacturers or that domestic manufacture is not commercially feasible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waivers are case-by-case and require showing efforts to obtain domestic manufacture or proof of infeasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: March-in rights — statutory triggers (clause (j))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal agency has the right to require contractor/assignee/exclusive licensee to grant a license (nonexclusive, partially exclusive, or exclusive) to responsible applicants, or to grant such a license itself if contractor refuses, where the agency determines that (1) contractor/assignee has not taken or is not expected to take effective steps to achieve practical application in a reasonable time; (2) action is necessary to alleviate unmet health or safety needs; (3) action is necessary to meet public use requirements specified by Federal regulations and not reasonably satisfied by contractor/assignee/licensees; or (4) action is necessary because the U.S. manufacturing agreement required by paragraph (i) has not been obtained or waived or because an exclusive licensee is in breach of that agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: March-in is a remedial licensing tool limited to stated grounds and subject to procedural safeguards in 37 CFR 401.6 and supplemental agency regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special provisions for nonprofit contractors — assignment control
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonprofit contractors agree that rights to a subject invention in the U.S. may not be assigned without Federal agency approval, except where assignment is to an organization whose primary function is management of inventions, provided assignee will be subject to same provisions as the contractor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency approval preserves oversight of nonprofit-to-private transfers of invention rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special provisions for nonprofit contractors — inventor royalty sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonprofit contractors will share royalties collected on a subject invention with the inventor, including Federal employee co-inventors when agency deems appropriate, when subject invention is assigned in accordance with 35 U.S.C. 202(e) and 37 CFR 401.10.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventor compensation is required and federal co-inventor sharing may be implemented per agency determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special provisions for nonprofit contractors — use of residual royalties
rubrics_metrics.description: The balance of any royalties or income earned by the contractor with respect to subject inventions, after payment of expenses (including payments to inventors) incidental to administration of subject inventions, will be utilized for the support of scientific research or education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures nonprofit proceeds support institutional research/education missions rather than unrelated purposes.
